The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
Borrow Hindsight

I sometimes ask: “How would I respond to this once I understood it more clearly, in balance and with compassion?” Sometimes I see the situation differently, feel more like that wiser version of myself, or feel accompanied by them. More than one can happen together. This is a fallible perspective to borrow, not proof that a perfect Higher Self is waiting underneath everything.

That wiser person also understands why I cannot respond ideally right now. What care or practical help would they offer me? If I cannot enter their state, I can still choose the smallest honest response, boundary, or pause available now. I don’t have to pretend to feel differently.

I can also imagine a wiser future version of the other person without assuming they will agree with me or regret what they did. Their potential does not replace the evidence of how they behave now.
note: Turn 65 (2026-10-17): Simple Practices, Borrow Hindsight, the E181 way.
length: two paragraphs, about 120 to 150 words together
before: (The end of The Inner Guide Comes Later; this is the first paragraph of a new h1, # Simple Practices, under ## Borrow Hindsight.)
brief:
- the main point: borrow your wiser self's hindsight: ask how you'd respond once you understood the situation more clearly, in balance and with compassion; it can change how you see it, or how you feel (more like that self, or accompanied); it's a fallible view, not proof of a perfect Higher Self; that wiser self also understands why you can't respond ideally now, so ask what care or practical help it would offer; you can imagine the other person's wiser future self too, without assuming they'll agree with you or regret anything.
- what the dedup leaves to add (experiments/t65-guide/SP-DEDUP-REPORT.md, G1): the hindsight question and how it lands; fallible, no perfect Higher Self; its grasp of your present limits; asking it for care or help; the other person's wiser future self, assuming no agreement or regret.
- already in the article, so not said again: the smallest honest response, boundary or pause ("start with the Protector's plain acts"); not pretending to feel ("pretend to feel anything"); potential vs present behavior ("what they keep showing you they can do").
- E159: the guide's "I sometimes ask" is a practice claim in the AI guide's first person, not Joel's words; say it as a practice for the reader.
